About Us

Our Farm

Vermont Shepherd is a family owned and operated 250-acre sheep farm in Westminster West, Vermont and is one of the oldest sheep dairies in the country. Here we raise 300-700 sheep (depending on the time of year), milk our flock of 250, and make a variety of aged and fresh cheeses and dairy products. We utilize intensive rotational grazing to feed and care for our sheep which promotes health, sustainability, and many other environmental benefits. Please visit us at our self-serve farm stand if you're ever in the neighborhood and enjoy our cheese!

Work on the farm includes: milking the sheep twice a day (5 a.m. and 5 p.m.), moving the sheep from pasture to pasture, haying, shearing sheep, cleaning to keep everything beautiful, and boxing up our cheeses and other goods and sending them out all over the country.

Vermont Shepherd has won two conservation awards in 2002 and 2006 for the quality of its farming work and improving the soils, pastures, and water resources. 

Our Sheep

Over the years our flock ewes, their rams, and hundreds of lambs have raised us to satisfy their every need. They require that we stay up all night during birthing to attend to breach births, plugged teats, or the occasional preemie, and to make a cozy corner of hay for each new mom and her lambs. Later, they employ us shepherds to run a lamb day care on the big flat field after the lambs have grown out of their cute stage and have become annoying, boisterous adolescents. At winter’s end, the sheep’s schedule for us includes a hair job (shearing), and a pedicure (hoof trim). Come summer, the ewes baa for us to make a new pasture after each milking, two pastures for each day of every month. In exchange, the sheep care for us, giving wool to keep us warm, milk and meat so we may live a long life and produce young shepherds who will be here to meet the sheeps’ needs for generations to come.

The Cheese Cave

Our cool and humid cave built into the side of a hill here at the farm offers ideal conditions for cheese ripening. Soon after the cheeses are made, we bring them to the cheese cave to be salted and ripened. During the 2-6 months ripening process, the cheeses rest on wooden boards and are carefully tended to by The Cave's affineur (French for cheese ripener.) The affineur turns and brushes each wheel every other day until flavor develops to the fullest.

The Vermont Shepherd Cheese Cave is home to over 20,000 lbs a year of our artisanal, farmhouse cheeses. This man-made cave is over 4' underground and is naturally damp and cool, the perfect conditions for cheese ripening!

All of our cheeses are aged on wooden boards, an age-old method that helps in the development of natural cheese rinds. Each day we turn, brush or wash the cheeses to cultivate beautiful, natural cheese rinds. These rinds, free of plastic and wax, help to enhance the cheeses' flavor and give our cheeses their unique characteristics.

Shipping & Returns
Shipping

We can ship to any destination in the United States. We ship via UPS and USPS Postal Priority (3-day delivery) Monday-Wednesday to be received by Friday. Because our product is perishable, we may delay your requested ship date to avoid weekend days in transit. Orders received after noon on Wednesday will not be shipped until the following Monday. 

For packages being shipped West of the Mississippi (any states WEST of MN, IA, MO, TN, and AL - FL is included also) please give us a postal address as the shipping address since we can now ship via Postal Priority flat rate, 2 - 3 day delivery.

Rush Delivery: If you would like your order shipped faster than the norm, please call 802-387-4473 or email us at vermontshepherd@gmail.com.

Schedule Delivery: If you would like your order to be shipped on a specific date, please call 802-387-4473 or email us at vermontshepherd@gmail.com

Our aged cheese is cured at 58 degrees F for at least 4 months. It should arrive at your door at cool room temperature (55 to 68 degrees).  Please refrigerate once it arrives.
Returns Policy

If you need to return an item, call us at 802-387-4473. We'll notify you via e-mail of your refund once we've received and processed the returned item.

Our Cheeses

Summer Cheese, Winter Cheese - Verano y Invierno

Like many fine foods… strawberries, cider, and asparagus, Vermont Shepherd cheeses are seasonal. Our summer cheese, “Verano,” we make from pure sheeps’ milk when our pastures are abundant with wild herbs and grasses. Verano then ages 3-5 months and ripens by August. The flavor of the summer cheese is sweet, rich and earthy with hints of clover, mint, and thyme. Our winter cheese, “Invierno,” we make from a mix of our sheeps’ milk and rich, organic milk from our neighbors cows. Invierno ages 5-9 months and ripens by early winter. The flavor of the winter cheese is strong and full, with a spicy tang. We sell the summer and winter cheeses by the pound and by the 6 to 8 lb wheel. We offer the 5-9 month aged Invierno, a reserve two year aged Invierno, as well as an apple wood smoked Invierno that is smoked with local apple wood. 

Fresh Cheeses 

In addition to our original aged cheeses, we also make a variety of fresh products with our sheep's milk. These include sheep's milk fromage blanc, a soft, rich, and creamy farmers' cheese reminiscent of cream cheese, sheep's milk ricotta, sheep's milk Skyr or Icelandic yogurt cheese, as well as a marinated fresh sheep's cheese with farm grown garlic and thyme, pure olive oil, and rainbow peppercorns.

2022 Workshop Series

***Our 2022 workshop series has come to a close and we do not have current plans to offer this series again. However, we did create corresponding workbooks for each of these workshops that contain the information that we covered in person. Please reach out to us if you would like a copy of the workbooks, and let us know if you would like to be on our workshop mailing list for updates about future workshops. Below is the information on each of the workshops that were offered:

Vermont Shepherd, one of the country's oldest and most well known sheep dairies, invites you to a series of 5 workshops in which we will explore how to successfully raise and farm dairy sheep in the northeast. With our collected knowledge of over 30 years in this industry and the help of additional experts, you will learn from start to finish how to begin a new venture or improve upon and innovate your existing business. This is a free workshop series that is made possible by the Northeast Dairy Business Innovation Center. This series consists of five workshops:

Lambing on a Sheep Dairy - in this workshop you will learn and experience first-hand the basics and nuances of birthing and caring for newborn lambs and their mothers. 
Milking on a Sheep Dairy - workshop covers training sheep to use the milking parlor, milking start to finish, and troubleshooting. We will also cover food safety and sanitation, and mastitis.  
Pasture Management for Dairy Sheep (with guest speaker Amber Reed) - in this workshop you will learn about rotational grazing for dairy sheep, managing pasture land, water and fencing systems, and the environmental and nutritional benefits of working this way with the land. Guest speaker Amber Reed will also be co-hosting this workshop. Amber is a grazing and pasture management specialist.   
Dairy Sheep Health (with guest speaker Dr. Stephen Major) - learn all about parasite and disease management, breeding, and overall sheep health. This workshop will be partially led by guest host Dr. Stephen Major, an animal health expert and local large animal veterinarian. 
Processing and Marketing Sheep Milk - this workshop covers how to profit off of your final product - sheep milk. We will have guest speakers from local businesses that buy and utilize sheep milk. This is a great opportunity to network and meet potential buyers of your product, and to learn options and methods for processing your own milk.

Visit Our Farm Store

 

Visit our Farm Store, purchase our cheese, and soak up the beautiful Vermont countryside. The farm store is open 7 days a week from 7am to 7pm. Our cheese is seasonal and thus so are the offerings in our farm store. But generally, we carry yarn, soap, shirts, maple syrup, Verano (100% sheep milk cheese), Invierno (cow and sheep mixed milk cheese), Ricotta Lana, plain and marinaded Fromage Blanc fresh cheese, and accompaniments for the various cheeses. 

Because we are busy farming and making cheese, visitors are discouraged from visiting our farm and facilities unless you have called ahead and made arrangements. The farm store is a great way to get a "taste" of what our farm and cheese is all about. We appreciate your understanding! 

Our farm store, located near beautiful sheep pastures, offers a great way to pick up a wedge or two of our cheese year round.  

When are the cheeses available? 

The supply of Vermont Shepherd Cheese is limited. While we make Invierno year-round, the Verano is hand made during the spring and summer months and then ages for 4 to 8 months. Invierno is available most of the year, while Verano is available from late August until the year's supply runs out in the spring.

Are visitors welcome? 

Visitors purchase our cheeses and other products at our Farm Store located on the road into our farm, the first little yellow building you come to on the right hand side. The store is open 7am-7pm, 7 days a week, year round. If you would like to tour our farm please call ahead to make arrangements so we can make sure someone is available for you.
